jobs.prompt: Write a change order to the Project Swarm roadmap scope: a new stage S9 Cluster, plus its design and benchmark document. Two files: (1) edit docs/scope/roadmap.md: add the line "- S9: Cluster (N devices, one ledger, autonomous node-to-node work)" to the Stages list after S8, and append a new section "## S9 Cluster" at the end with requirements R-050 to R-061, written in exactly the style of the existing sections (a heading "### R-0NN Sentence." then "Acceptance:" and 3 to 5 bullet lines each, every line checkable: a command, a number, an exit code or a visible result). Do not change any existing text; R-048 and R-049 stay as they are (S9 builds on R-048: say so in the Overview-free first acceptance line of R-051 instead of editing R-048). (2) create docs/architecture/cluster.md: the cluster design with these sections: Goal; Nodes and the node registry; The shared ledger and leases (claim, heartbeat, expiry, work stealing, why double builds cannot happen: a single atomic claim record with a fencing token that every write must present, a lease that expires only by the ledger owner clock, never by a node clock); Transport (a persistent connection over the tailnet, per-node signed typed messages, GitHub swarm-inbox fallback only while a peer is offline, replay protection with per-sender monotonic sequence numbers and a nonce window); Message schema (typed only: handoff, ticket-done, release-shipped, request, question, ack, plus lease-claim, lease-heartbeat, lease-release, node-hello; every message is data validated against a JSON schema, never executable, no free-form commands, size cap, secret scan on send and on receive, no keys or tokens ever in a message); Trust boundary (owner-only actions stay owner-only on every node: approve, merge to live, deploy, caps, spend, keys; a message can never perform or imply any of them; a message that tries is dropped, logged and raised to the owner); Failure model (node dies mid-ticket, network drops, clock skew, two nodes claim at once, partition healing, duplicate delivery); Benchmarks (the table below, how each is measured, where results are stored per release, the CI regression gate); Stages C1 to C6 with a gate for each; Risks and what is deliberately not built (no multi-owner trust, no remote code execution, no auto-update of peers). Requirements to cover (one R each, in this order): R-050 Any machine joins with swarm join using tailnet auth and appears in the node registry with capabilities (cores, RAM, lanes, GPU, machine limit); R-051 One shared ledger with ticket leases replaces hand-offs (claim with lease, heartbeat, automatic expiry returns a dead node ticket to the pool, fencing token, never a double build); R-052 Work stealing: a node with free slots pulls ready tickets, honoring ticket target worktree, file ownership, lane and capability fit, and fair share across projects; R-053 Event push over the tailnet on a persistent connection, with the GitHub swarm-inbox fallback only while a peer is offline, and a message wakes the receiving orchestrator or autopilot as an event; R-054 Typed, schema-validated, per-node signed messages, never executable, secret scan on send, replay protection, forged-sender rejection; R-055 Autonomous flow: ticket-done, release-shipped, handoff, request, question and ack flow between nodes with no owner relay, and owner-only actions (approve, merge to live, deploy, caps, spend, keys) stay owner-only on every node, a message can never do them; R-056 swarm msg send, list and tail commands and swarm node list, plus the board message log and node view for every machine; R-057 Benchmarks run for each release against a fixed baseline and results are stored per release; R-058 CI fails when a benchmark regresses past a threshold and the trend shows on Swarm Watch; R-059 Chaos tests: kill a node mid-ticket, drop the network, clock skew, two nodes claiming at once; R-060 The MacBook and the Mac mini are the first two nodes and the existing hand-off flow (branches, relayed messages) is retired once both run on the ledger; R-061 Nodes of any number work: a third node joins and leaves without breaking leases or the board (test with three simulated nodes). Benchmark targets to state in the doc and in the acceptance lines (numbers exactly): message latency p50 under 100 ms and p95 under 1 s on the tailnet; ticket ready to started time p95 under 30 s when a node has a free slot; slot utilization across all nodes above 80 percent whenever ready tickets exist; idle node-minutes while ready tickets exist at about 0 (under 1 percent of node-minutes); owner relays needed 0; double-claims 0 (any double claim fails the release); throughput measured as tickets done per hour per node, recorded and trended (regression gate: more than 10 percent worse than the stored baseline fails CI; latency p95 more than 25 percent worse fails CI; utilization more than 5 points worse fails CI). Results are stored per release as one JSON file per version under bench/cluster/ (schema in the doc), produced by a deterministic simulated-cluster harness (injected clock and fake transport) so CI is stable, plus an optional real-tailnet run for the owner. Stages C1 to C6 in the doc, each with its gate: C1 node registry and swarm join (gate: two nodes visible in swarm node list within 5 s), C2 typed signed messages with the secret scan and the forged-sender, replay and approve-attempt tests (gate: all three tests pass), C3 shared ledger with leases and fencing (gate: 1000 simulated two-node claim races, 0 double claims), C4 push transport with the fallback and the wake event (gate: p95 under 1 s in the harness), C5 work stealing, autonomy flows and the board log (gate: a ticket built on node B is marked delivered on node A with no owner action), C6 benchmarks, CI gate and chaos suite (gate: the four chaos scenarios pass, the baseline is stored). Two existing tests read the real roadmap (tests/build-progress-roadmap.test.mjs and tests/build-progress-ledgers.test.mjs): run them after the edit; if one asserts a fixed requirement count or stage list that the new stage legitimately changes, update only that expectation with a comment, never loosen anything else. Keep the whole document under 400 lines. Plain words, no marketing. No secrets, no real keys, no real addresses. The roadmap edit must keep `swarm scope check docs/scope/roadmap.md` valid: run it if possible, otherwise verify every requirement has a heading and an Acceptance list.
